title: Разговор на воздухе  (A Talk Outside in the Fresh Air)

segments.t: Terrified by Nastya's sudden affectionate behavior, Kostya runs into the kitchen begging for help. Right behind him, Max appears yet again, and Senya and Fedya persuade Chef Barinov to simply step outside with Max and listen to what he has to say so he will finally leave.
Шеф, шеф, шеф, это не поможет.
Шеф, я не хотел предавать вас.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'I already love you so much as it is...' Barinov brings a direct mood right away, building the phrase around "ochen" ("very much") and "mne" ("to me") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Kostyan, save me right now!' Max displays a sharp direction in the scene, combining "spasay" ("save") and "kostyan" ("Kostyan") so the key meaning lands right away.
'I warned you not to come in here!' Kostya shares a warm posture right away, pairing "preduprezhdal" ("warned") with "ya" ("I") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Nastya, wait, we will talk about it later.' Barinov takes an unhurried stance straight away, using "podozhdi" (from "podozhdat", "wait") alongside "potom" ("then") to shape the meaning.
Шеф, шеф, шеф, это не поможет.
'Chef, Chef, Chef, chasing him will not help.' Max shows a serious style in the scene, using "pomozhet" (from "pomoch", "will help") alongside "shef" ("Chef") to shape the meaning.
'I know him very well.' Kostya sets a warm manner without hesitation, leaning on "ochen" ("very much") before closing the thought with "khorosho" ("good, fine").
'It is better if you simply hear him out.' Barinov adopts a brisk view during the exchange, pairing "luchshe" ("better") with "prosto" ("just") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Chef, please, just talk to him for a minute.' Max holds a natural posture straight away, weaving "prosto" ("just") together with "pogovorite" ("have a word") just the way native speakers do.

'Alright, let us step outside for some air.' Kostya shows a candid position in the scene, building the phrase around "davay" ("let's") and "vyydem" ("to go out, to get out") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Шеф, я не хотел предавать вас.
'Chef, I never wanted to betray you.' Max establishes a pointed position on the spot, leaning on "khotel" ("wanted") before closing the thought with "predavat" ("to betray").

'I simply could not have acted any other way.' Max offers a calm line as the scene unfolds, building the phrase around "mog" ("can, to be able") and "postupit" ("get into") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'You made your own choice yourself.' Kostya displays a resolute rhythm toward Max, putting "sdelal" ("did") alongside "vybor" ("choice") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'And only after that come all the money issues.' Barinov brings a natural view in this beat, pairing "potom" ("then") with "babki" ("grand") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Шеф, шеф, шеф, это не поможет.
Шеф, я не хотел предавать вас.
That wraps up this scene as spooked by Nastya's sweetness, Kostya begs the cooks for help, while Senya and Fedya convince Chef Barinov to step outside and hear Max out one last time. Until next time!
